question: Can a workspace assembled from independently updated sources be chronologically fresh yet contain mixed logical epochs?

construction.coupled_underlying_updates: Poisson process; each conceptual state update should be seen as one epoch by all six sources
construction.per_source_propagation_delay: independent uniform [0,2] ms per conceptual update
construction.read_offsets: six evenly spaced positions across the 0.6 ms span
construction.validation_arm: accept only if all six source epoch witnesses agree; otherwise retry/escalate

interpretation: Freshness and consistency are distinct. In the constructed coupled-update workload, a low-latency sequential read can still combine source epochs. Version witnesses reject such mixed frames at a retry cost equal to their occurrence rate.
boundary: Not a FRANK runtime measurement. Update rates, propagation delays and the assumption of coupled source epochs are constructed. The current architecture source does not specify whether baue_broadcast(q) already receives an atomic snapshot; this experiment motivates live instrumentation rather than claiming a production bug.
falsifier_or_next_test: Instrument current FRANK q/workspace inputs with per-channel source revisions. If live frames are already atomically assembled or no incompatible mixed revisions occur, the proposed CognitiveFrame consistency gate may be unnecessary or reducible.
